Chronic Abscess: The patient presents with a two-week history of asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face, gross right facial asymmetry, and a 6 × 6 cm ovid subcutaneous swelling. The contrast-enhanced CT of the face showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space, which is consistent with a chronic abscess. The patient's history of similar episodes and the presence of swelling also support this diagnosis.
Buccal Space Infection: The patient has elevated and glistening right buccal mucosa, restricted mouth opening, and erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla, which are consistent with a buccal space infection. The presence of facial swelling and limited mouth opening also support this diagnosis.
